statement: ZIP adapter is an independent hand-written parser, deliberately not using a ZIP library; central, local and data-descriptor claims are kept as separate observations until the strict resolver classifies them.
research_needed: Differential fuzzing against libarchive/Python/Java readers to confirm independent parser does not miss structures.

statement: ZIP signatures and recognised field constants: EOCD, ZIP64 locator/EOCD, central, local, descriptor; extras ZIP64 0x0001, NTFS 0x000a, extended timestamp 0x5455, Info-ZIP Unicode Path 0x7075 and Comment 0x6375; flags UTF-8 bit 11, descriptor bit 3, encrypted bit 0, strong-encryption bit 6.

ZipImportPolicy is a public caller-owned struct of 15 limits: archive bytes, entries, central-directory bytes, extra bytes, name/comment bytes, per-entry compressed/uncompressed bytes, total uncompressed, expansion ratio (milli), observations, observations per subject, conflicts, resolutions, conversion-record bytes, preserved-source bytes.

Default ZIP limits: archive 4 GiB, 1,000,000 entries, CD 256 MiB, extras 64 MiB, names/comments 64 MiB, entry compressed 2 GiB, entry uncompressed 4 GiB, total 16 GiB, ratio 1000:1, 8M observations, 4096 per subject, 1M conflicts, 1M resolutions, 256 MiB evidence, 4 GiB preserved source. No measurement cited.
research_needed: Measure real-world ZIP corpus distribution (entries, sizes, ratios, jar/docx/apk/npm) and peak memory under defaults; confirm defaults refuse bombs without refusing legitimate archives.
decision_needed: Are the default ZIP import limits the frozen v1 defaults, and are they user-tunable from the CLI?

statement: ZIP expansion ratio default 1,000,000 milli (1000:1) differs from 7z default max_expansion_ratio 10,000 (10000:1, not milli); the two adapters use different units and different bounds for the same bomb-defence concept.
research_needed: Measure legitimate max compression ratios (sparse images, zero-filled VM disks, logs) in ZIP and 7z corpora; harmonise units.
decision_needed: Should legacy adapters share one expansion-ratio unit and default, and what value?

statement: ZIP compatibility import v1 supports exactly four frozen runtime profiles: zip/python-zipfile@3.13.5, zip/java-zipfile@21.0.12.1, zip/java-zipinputstream@21.0.12.1, zip/libarchive-bsdtar@3.8.8.
evidence_in_source: doc comment 'Frozen runtime behavior contracts'; matrix in tools/zip-compat (not loaded by code)
research_needed: Re-validate profile rules against tools/zip-compat/observed-outcomes-v1.json mechanically in CI; decide whether .NET ZipArchive, Go archive/zip, 7-Zip, Windows Explorer, macOS Archive Utility, Info-ZIP unzip need profiles.
decision_needed: Which additional runtimes (e.g. .NET, Go, 7-Zip, Explorer, Archive Utility, unzip) require frozen compatibility profiles for v1?

statement: Profile IDs parse only by exact string match; unknown or unversioned IDs fail with UnsupportedRequiredFeature (Unsupported). Unversioned aliases are therefore refused.
evidence_in_source: code; CLI test preserve_requires_an_exact_compatibility_profile (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs L5517-5537) checks '--compat=zip/java' refusal

statement: ImportPolicy enum has Strict, Compatibility(profile), Preservation(profile); Preservation always requires a compatibility profile (no strict preservation); mode strings are strict/compat/preserve.
There is no Preservation variant without a compatibility profile, so exact-source preservation is unavailable for strictly imported ZIPs; the type system forbids strict+preserve.
evidence_in_source: enum shape; CLI refuses '--preserve' without '--compat' (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs L1807-1815, L2083-2091)
decision_needed: Should --preserve be allowed with strict reconciliation, or is preservation intentionally coupled to a compatibility profile?

statement: Public result types: ZipConversionReport (LOM observation, resolutions, synthesized ancestors) and ZipImportResult (native Archive + report). ZipObservation exposes only lom(); source bytes and structural entries are private so callers cannot bypass reconciliation.

observe() requires source <= max_archive_bytes, computes SHA-256 of whole source, and locates EOCD by reverse scan of the final 65,557 bytes for a signature whose comment length ends exactly at EOF; the highest-offset EOF-aligned candidate wins.

EOCD search accepts the last EOF-aligned signature without recording competing EOCD candidates (e.g. a forged EOCD inside an archive comment) as a LOM conflict; EOCD ambiguity is not surfaced as an observation.
research_needed: Generate archives with multiple EOF-aligned EOCD candidates and compare Python/Java/libarchive; decide whether ambiguity is Irreconcilable.
decision_needed: Should multiple structurally valid EOCD candidates be an Irreconcilable conflict in strict mode?

statement: Any EOCD signature in the tail that does not align to EOF yields Truncated (ZipStructureInvalid); the separate 'comment length does not identify an exact EOF record' structure branch appears unreachable because the partial scan also matches complete signatures.
research_needed: Add a test for a non-EOF-aligned complete EOCD to confirm Truncated vs Corrupt outcome class.

statement: Input without any EOCD signature is refused with Unsupported LegacyFormatUnsupported ('not structurally recognizable as ZIP').
EOCD comment must end exactly at EOF and archive comment length counts against max_name_comment_bytes; trailing bytes after the EOCD comment are refused as structure errors.
Multi-disk/spanned ZIP is refused (ZipUnsupportedFeature): nonzero disk numbers, mismatched entries-on-disk, multi-disk ZIP64 locator/EOCD, or nonzero entry disk_start.
research_needed: Measure prevalence of split/spanned ZIP (.z01) in user corpora.
decision_needed: Is split/spanned ZIP import a v1 non-goal or post-v1 adapter work?

statement: ZIP64 directory is parsed only when an EOCD field holds a sentinel (0xFFFF entries or 0xFFFFFFFF size/offset); the locator must directly precede EOCD and the ZIP64 EOCD must end exactly at the locator with body length >= 44.

Any bytes between central directory end and EOCD are refused as unsupported, including a ZIP64 EOCD/locator emitted when no EOCD sentinel requires it and the central-directory digital signature record.
research_needed: Survey writers that always emit ZIP64 records (Info-ZIP zip -fz, some Java/.NET/streaming writers) and signed ZIPs; measure refusal rate.
decision_needed: Should unconditional ZIP64 end records and CD digital-signature records be accepted as observations in strict v1?

statement: ZIP64 EOCD extensible data sector (body length > 44) is accepted but neither interpreted nor recorded as an observation.
research_needed: Check whether any writer populates the extensible data sector; decide whether bytes must be observed for preservation completeness.

statement: Archive-scope LOM fields recorded with exact byte evidence: EOCD disk numbers, entry counts, CD size/offset, ZIP64 locator EOCD offset, ZIP64 entry count/CD size/offset, and archive comment bytes.
When ZIP64 is used, each non-sentinel ZIP32 EOCD value that differs from its ZIP64 counterpart is recorded as a Divergence conflict (entry_count, central_directory_size, central_directory_offset).
Entry count and CD size must respect policy, the CD must lie before EOCD within the source, and walking entry_count central records must consume exactly the declared CD extent.

For each central record the parser follows its local-header offset, parses local header, checks flags, compares central/local header and extra claims, enforces size/ratio policy, bounds file data before the CD, parses an optional descriptor, and builds per-entry LOM fields.

Strict ZIP does not require the first local header at offset 0, contiguous entries, or explained gaps; prefix data (e.g. self-extracting stubs without offset fix-up) and inter-entry gaps are neither refused nor recorded, unlike the 7z adapter which refuses unexplained bytes.
research_needed: Build cases with prepended stubs, gaps and hidden data between entries; compare reader behaviour and decide whether unexplained bytes are Omission/Irreconcilable evidence.
decision_needed: Must strict ZIP import report or refuse unexplained bytes (prefix, gaps) as it does for 7z?

statement: Expansion-ratio policy is evaluated on declared central sizes (uncompressed*1000/compressed); a zero compressed size with nonzero uncompressed size is treated as infinite ratio and refused.
evidence_in_source: test unsafe_paths_and_resource_bombs_are_refused (L3927-3975) covers per-entry size limit only
research_needed: Adversarial test where declared sizes are small but DEFLATE output is large, under strict and each compat profile.

statement: Unsupported-metadata classes collected from observation: zip.archive.comment, zip.entry.comment, zip.platform-attributes (nonzero internal/external attributes), zip.entry.unicode-comment, zip.ntfs-timestamps, and zip.extra.<id> for every unrecognised extra field.
research_needed: Enumerate common extras (0x7875 Unix UID/GID, 0x5855, 0x756e ASi Unix, 0x9901 AES, 0xcafe JAR, 0xd935 Android alignment) and decide which map to EAM metadata.
decision_needed: Which ZIP extra fields (UID/GID, Unix mode, symlink, APK alignment) must be interpreted into EAM for v1?

statement: Encrypted ZIP entries (traditional PKWARE bit 0 or strong-encryption bit 6) are refused at observation with ZipUnsupportedFeature; there is no password/AES-ZIP decryption.
research_needed: Measure share of encrypted ZIPs (ZipCrypto, WinZip AES 0x9901) in migration targets; security review of any decrypt path.
decision_needed: Is encrypted-ZIP import (ZipCrypto/WinZip AES) in or out of v1 migration scope?

statement: Only compression methods 0 (STORE) and 8 (DEFLATE) are supported; any other method (Deflate64, bzip2, LZMA, Zstandard, XZ, PPMd, WinZip AES 99, etc.) refuses the whole archive at observation.
research_needed: Corpus measurement of ZIP method distribution (Deflate64 from Windows Explorer >2GB, zstd 93 from newer 7-Zip/WinZip, LZMA 14).
decision_needed: Which additional ZIP methods (Deflate64, zstd, LZMA, bzip2) must strict v1 decode?

statement: General-purpose flags outside UTF-8 (bit 11), descriptor (bit 3) and compression options (bits 1-2) are refused, including enhanced deflate bit 4, patched data bit 5, masked local headers bit 13 and reserved bits.
research_needed: Check whether any mainstream writer sets reserved/other bits (e.g. bit 1-2 variants, bit 12) on benign archives.

statement: Unsupported methods, encryption, flags and disk numbers are checked during observe() and abort the whole observation for a single bad entry; there is no per-entry refusal or partial import, and the refusal never enters the LOM.
research_needed: Usability study: whether users expect partial conversion with a FidelityReport listing skipped entries.
decision_needed: Should unsupported entries be skipped with evidence (LOSSY) or always refuse the whole archive?

statement: Central records are parsed from a 46-byte fixed header plus name, extras and comment; ZIP64 extra values replace only sentinel-valued sizes, offset and disk; central claims carry version-made-by, internal and external attributes.

Local headers are parsed independently; when descriptor flag is set, zero-valued local CRC and sizes are treated as omitted (None) rather than as zero claims; local headers never carry attributes, disk or offset.

ZIP64 extra handling: duplicate ZIP64 extras are Irreconcilable, a sentinel without a ZIP64 extra is a structure error, and a ZIP64 extra containing bytes beyond the values required by sentinels is refused as Divergence.

Local ZIP64 extras are read with only size sentinels as required values, so writers that emit a full or zero-filled ZIP64 extra in local headers without 0xFFFFFFFF sentinels (common in streaming writers) would be refused as 'contradictory unrequested values'.
evidence_in_source: code reading; no test covers this
research_needed: Corpus/writer survey (Java ZipOutputStream, .NET, Go, libzip, Info-ZIP streaming, 7-Zip) for ZIP64 extras present without sentinels; measure strict refusal rate.
decision_needed: Should surplus ZIP64 extra values be accepted as Refinement/Omission evidence instead of refusing?

statement: Several structural contradictions (duplicate ZIP64 extra, surplus ZIP64 values, descriptor signature equal to CRC) are raised as hard diagnostics inside observe() rather than recorded as LOM conflicts, contradicting the module promise that claims stay observations until the resolver classifies them; compat profiles can never model them.
evidence_in_source: module doc L3-5 vs code; test descriptor_ambiguity expects ZipConflictIrreconcilable from observe (L3815-3835)
research_needed: Audit every observe()-time error against the four conflict classes; decide which become LOM conflicts.
decision_needed: Must all multi-authority contradictions be recorded in the LOM before refusal so preserve/compat can report them?

statement: Extra-field blocks must frame exactly within the header; truncated headers or data beyond the enclosing header are structure errors; per-entry extra count is bounded by max_observations_per_subject.

Data descriptors (flag bit 3) are parsed after the central-declared compressed extent; the signature is optional; ZIP64 descriptor width is chosen when central raw sizes are 0xFFFFFFFF; a descriptor whose leading value equals both the signature and the central CRC is Irreconcilable.

Descriptor ZIP64 width is inferred only from central sentinels; writers that use 64-bit descriptors while central sizes are non-sentinel (or vice versa) are parsed at the wrong width, producing divergence or extent errors.
research_needed: Generate descriptor-width variants from real streaming writers and compare outcomes.

statement: Central vs local comparisons: filename, flags, method and DOS date/time differences are Divergence; optional CRC, sizes, attributes, disk and offset produce Divergence when both present and Omission (resolved to the sole declaration) when only central declares them.

Every entry emits Omission conflicts for internal_attributes, external_attributes, disk_start and local_header_offset because local headers structurally lack them (plus three more for descriptor entries); with default max_conflicts and max_resolutions of 1,000,000, archives above roughly 250,000 entries would be policy-refused despite max_entries 1,000,000.
evidence_in_source: code reading; no test imports more than two entries
research_needed: Import generated ZIPs with 100k/300k/1M entries; measure conflicts, resolutions, ConversionProvenance encoded bytes (256 MiB cap) and AUX record size per entry.
decision_needed: Should structurally absent local fields be excluded from conflicts, and should per-entry resolutions be aggregated to bound ConversionProvenance size?

statement: Extra-field ID sets are compared across central/local: IDs present in only one header are Omission (retain available evidence), same IDs with different bytes are Refinement (both encodings retained; semantics compared after decoding).
Descriptor CRC and sizes are compared with central claims; any difference is a Divergence conflict (field names crc32, compressed_size, uncompressed_size).
Overlapping physical entry extents (local header start to data or descriptor end, sorted by offset) are Irreconcilable and refused with ZipOverlappingExtent in every import mode.
research_needed: Test overlapping-file quines (Fifield 'better zip bomb') and shared local headers.

statement: Strict resolution refuses any Irreconcilable conflict (ZipOverlappingExtent or ZipConflictIrreconcilable) and then any Divergence conflict (ZipConflictDivergence); diagnostics include divergence and irreconcilable counts.

Strict entry resolution: local and central names must match, attribute-derived kind must agree with trailing-slash marker, directories must declare zero size, content is decoded from the central compressed extent, length must equal central uncompressed size and CRC-32 must match central CRC.

Strict decoding: STORE requires compressed length equal to declared size; DEFLATE output is capped at min(declared, policy) plus one byte, preallocation capped at 16 MiB, and the stream must consume exactly its compressed extent.

Strict name resolution: UTF-8 flag selects UTF-8 (invalid bytes are ZipAmbiguousName); otherwise CP437 decoding; CRC-bound Info-ZIP Unicode Path extras refine a CP437 name (Refinement) but disagreeing extras or disagreement with a UTF-8-flagged name are refused as ambiguous.

A Unicode Path extra with wrong version, stale CRC, or invalid UTF-8 causes refusal (ZipAmbiguousName) rather than being ignored in favour of the primary name, which APPNOTE-conforming readers do for stale extras.
research_needed: Measure frequency of stale Unicode Path extras (renamed entries by tools that do not update 0x7075) and reader behaviour.
decision_needed: Should a CRC-mismatched Unicode Path extra be ignored (Omission) instead of refusing?

statement: Names without the UTF-8 flag or valid Unicode extra are always decoded as CP437; no other legacy code page (Shift_JIS, GBK, CP866, CP1252 via OEM locale) can be selected, so archives from non-Western Windows locales are mis-decoded deterministically.
research_needed: Corpus study of non-UTF-8 ZIP names by locale; evaluate explicit --zip-name-encoding option versus raw-byte path preservation.
decision_needed: Should ZIP import accept an explicit legacy code-page override or preserve raw name bytes as non-UTF-8 path components?

statement: ZIP path safety: NUL, leading '/' or '\', any backslash, leading drive letter, empty name, empty components, '.' and '..' are refused with ZipUnsafePath; trailing '/' marks a directory.

ZIP adapter refuses backslash names outright and does not refuse ':' inside components, whereas the 7z adapter normalises backslash to '/' and refuses colon components as alternate streams; adapter path policies diverge.
research_needed: Measure Windows-created ZIPs with backslash separators; define one legacy path policy for ':' and '\' across adapters.
decision_needed: Should legacy adapters share one separator/colon policy, and should ZIP backslash names be normalised or refused?

statement: Unix-host ZIP entries (version-made-by host 3) whose mode type is not regular or directory (symlink, FIFO, device, socket) are refused with ZipUnsupportedFeature in strict mode; symlink import is unsupported.
research_needed: Measure symlink prevalence in ZIPs (macOS app bundles, Android, npm) and assess EAM symlink support.
decision_needed: Will v1 map ZIP symlinks into EAM symlink entries or keep refusing?

statement: Directory kind also comes from MS-DOS attribute bit 0x10; executable is set only when host is Unix and any of mode bits 0o111 is set; other permission bits are not imported.
research_needed: Decide whether full POSIX mode from ZIP external attributes should populate platform metadata.

statement: Strict mtime: local/central DOS timestamps must match; mtime comes only from NTFS extra (100 ns, preferred) or extended timestamp 0x5455 mtime (seconds, i32), each recorded as Refinement; the two must agree to the second; DOS time alone yields no mtime.
DOS timestamps are never imported because they lack a UTC offset; most ZIPs carry only DOS time, so their mtimes are dropped (FidelityReport zip.dos-mtime) with no option to assume a zone.
research_needed: Measure fraction of ZIPs lacking UT/NTFS extras; usability test of losing mtimes; evaluate --assume-timezone option.
decision_needed: Should DOS local timestamps be importable with an explicit, recorded timezone assumption?

statement: Access/creation times in 0x5455 and NTFS extras are silently discarded: 0x5455 is not listed as unsupported metadata, and although mtime is captured from these extras the ZIP FidelityReport captured list omits core.mtime while listing zip.ntfs-timestamps as unavailable.
research_needed: Add fidelity tests asserting captured/unavailable classes for UT and NTFS extras.

statement: NTFS extra parsing requires tag 1 attribute of exactly 24 bytes (three FILETIMEs) and converts the first (mtime) with correct flooring for pre-1970 ticks; truncated attributes are structure errors.
research_needed: Add unit tests for pre-1970 and far-future NTFS FILETIMEs (none exist).

statement: Strict ZIP import refuses duplicate reconciled logical paths with DuplicateLogicalPath (Nonconforming).
Under compat/preserve every profile resolves duplicate paths by keeping the later member (in central-directory order) and records a Divergence resolution stating extraction safety remains enforced.
evidence_in_source: code; no unit test exercises duplicate paths under compat
research_needed: Add compat duplicate-path tests; verify against observed matrix, especially Java ZipInputStream which the profile document says processes local order.

statement: Compat duplicate resolution iterates entries in central-directory ordinal order for all profiles, so for zip/java-zipinputstream (documented as local-order processing) the 'last' duplicate may differ when local order differs from central order.
research_needed: Generate duplicate members with reordered central directory; compare Java ZipInputStream observed result to Entrybound compat output.

statement: Missing directory ancestors are synthesized as explicit Directory entries with empty metadata and recorded as Omission resolutions; a file acting as an ancestor is refused with FileAsAncestor.

EAM projection: files become Internal content refs by SHA-256 of plaintext with metadata executable plus optional mtime; directories carry the same metadata; identical content deduplicates to one content object.

ConversionProvenance for ZIP: adapter_id 'zip-strict/v1' or the compat profile ID, import_mode, source SHA-256, entry and observation counts, omission/refinement/divergence/irreconcilable counts, sorted deduplicated resolutions, synthesized ancestors, unsupported metadata, outcome 'success'.
ZIP strict adapter ID 'zip-strict/v1' uses a different naming scheme from the 7z ID 'entrybound/sevenz-strict-v1'; adapter ID grammar is not unified.
decision_needed: What is the canonical adapter_id grammar for ConversionProvenance across all legacy adapters?

statement: Encoded conversion plus preservation evidence size (via ecf::encoded_legacy_evidence_len) must not exceed max_conversion_record_bytes (default 256 MiB) or import is policy-refused.
evidence_in_source: no test exercises the 256 MiB evidence cap directly

statement: Resolved ZIP content is handed to the ordinary native planner (plan_observed_archive) with the caller's CompressionProfile; output is a normal native Archive.

Conversion provenance affects only the AUX identity: LAI and PCR are identical with and without ConversionProvenance, and the FEATURE_CONVERSION_PROVENANCE_V1 bit must match record presence (DuplicateSemanticDeclaration otherwise); INDEXED and STREAM round-trip it.

ZIP FidelityReport: platform 'legacy:zip'; captured core.executable and legacy.conversion-provenance; unavailable always includes zip.dos-mtime plus each unsupported metadata class; no degraded items.

Public entry points: observe(source, policy), resolve(observation, policy, profile, import_policy), resolve_strict(...), import_strict(source, policy, profile), import(source, policy, profile, import_policy); all operate on a complete in-memory byte slice.

ZIP import is fully in-memory: source slice plus a full copy inside ZipObservation, plus all decoded plaintext retained until planning; defaults permit 4 GiB source and 16 GiB total output, implying tens of GiB peak memory.
research_needed: Measure peak RSS importing 1 GiB/4 GiB ZIPs; evaluate streaming/mmap observation and bounded staging.
decision_needed: Must legacy import be bounded-memory (streaming or staged) for v1?

statement: Compat rules frozen per profile: Python selects central name/method/sizes/CRC, requires name match, uses Unicode extra, enforces CRC and size, allows trailing DEFLATE bytes; Java ZipFile selects central values, ignores Unicode extra, enforces neither CRC nor declared size.
research_needed: Mechanically compare rule table with tools/zip-compat/observed-outcomes-v1.json in CI (no Rust test loads the matrix).

statement: Java ZipInputStream selects local name/method and descriptor sizes/CRC, enforces CRC and size, refuses trailing DEFLATE bytes; libarchive bsdtar selects local name with Unicode extra, requires local/central method/size/CRC agreement, enforces CRC and size, refuses trailing bytes, and derives directory kind from attributes.
research_needed: Same as above: CI check against observed-outcomes-v1.json; rerun probes on Linux/macOS builds of the same versions.

statement: Only the libarchive profile inspects attribute-derived entry kind; under Python and both Java profiles a Unix symlink/FIFO/device entry is not refused but imported as a regular file (symlink target as content, executable if mode 0o111), contrary to the documented safety override refusing special files.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/zip-compatibility-profiles-v1.md §Safety overrides L76-83 (code appears not to enforce special-file refusal for 3 profiles)
evidence_in_source: code reading; test compatibility_never_overrides_native_safety_or_evidence_budgets (L4420-4469) covers only '../escape' and preserved-source budget
research_needed: Add compat tests with 0o120777/0o010644 external attributes for every profile; security review of compat projection.
decision_needed: Must every compat profile refuse non-regular Unix entry types before projection?

statement: Compat-selected extents (local or descriptor compressed size) are only bounded by the source and central-directory start; overlap classification uses central-derived extents, so a selected local extent may read into another member's bytes without ZipOverlappingExtent.
evidence_in_source: code reading; docs claim reads beyond an observed compressed extent are refused
research_needed: Build a case with local compressed size larger than central for java-zipinputstream; check whether import reads the next header's bytes.
decision_needed: Should compat re-run overlap/extent validation on the profile-selected extents?

statement: Compat decoding bounds output only by max_uncompressed_entry_bytes (4 GiB); profiles that do not enforce declared size (java-zipfile) bypass the declared expansion-ratio check, so actual ratio is unbounded per entry until the 16 GiB total check.
research_needed: Bomb test: declared 1 KiB, DEFLATE to 4 GiB, under java-zipfile compat; measure memory/time.
decision_needed: Should compat decode enforce the expansion ratio on actual output?

statement: Profiles requiring name match refuse local/central filename mismatch; libarchive refuses divergent local/central method, compressed/uncompressed size and CRC, all with ZipConflictDivergence.

Compat records a Divergence ConversionResolution whenever central and local name or method differ, naming the selected authority and profile; a Unicode Path extra overriding the primary name is also recorded.

Compat directories get empty plaintext regardless of declared content; declared-size and CRC checks follow profile rules; a content Divergence resolution is recorded when declared and actual sizes differ or local/central CRC differ.
research_needed: Test compat directory entry with nonzero data under java-zipfile (content silently dropped).

statement: Compat mtime is resolved from the selected name header only (passed as both central and local), so the other header's timestamp extras are ignored; DOS time divergence is already refused as unmodeled.
Compat/preserve refuse all Irreconcilable conflicts with the message 'compatibility interpretation blocked by Entrybound safety invariant' (ZipOverlappingExtent or ZipConflictIrreconcilable).

Compat refuses any Divergence whose field is outside the modeled set {filename, compression_method, crc32, compressed_size, uncompressed_size}; e.g. flags, DOS time, attributes and ZIP32/ZIP64 EOCD divergences are refused as 'not modeled'.
research_needed: Measure how often real archives have local/central flag or DOS-time differences (e.g. bit 3 only in local); decide whether to model them.
decision_needed: Should flag and timestamp divergences be modeled by compat profiles?

statement: Preserve mode stores 'legacy-preservation/v1': exact source bytes, source digest, every archive and entry observation (scope, ordinals, raw/interpreted values, evidence, validity), every conflict, and the selected resolutions; source size limited by max_preserved_source_bytes.

Preservation changes AUX only (LAI/PCR equal to compat import); FEATURE_LEGACY_PRESERVATION_V1 must match record presence; tampered preserved source bytes fail encode with AuxMismatch; source is recoverable from INDEXED and STREAM layouts.

recover_preserved_source(archive) validates the archive, requires legacy-preservation evidence (else UnsupportedRequiredFeature) and that preserved bytes hash to both the preservation digest and ConversionProvenance source digest (else Corrupt AuxMismatch).

recover_preserved_source lives in the ZIP module although legacy-preservation/v1 is described as format-neutral; no 7z or tar preservation producer exists, and there is no CLI command to extract the preserved source in the slice.
decision_needed: Should preserved-source recovery be a format-neutral API and CLI command, and which adapters must support preserve?

statement: Preserve embeds the entire foreign source inside the native archive in addition to decoded content, roughly doubling archive size; no measurement of size or planner dedup interaction is present.
research_needed: Measure preserved archive size vs compat archive for representative ZIPs; test whether preserved source bytes are compressed/deduplicated.

statement: CLI convert and sidecar map flags to ImportPolicy: --strict and --compat are mutually exclusive, --preserve requires --compat; non-strict policies are available only for ZIP ('--compat and --preserve are currently defined only for ZIP') and always use ZipImportPolicy::default().
The CLI exposes no options to change ZIP or 7z import limits; LegacyImportPolicy::default() and ZipImportPolicy::default() are hard-wired.
decision_needed: Should CLI users be able to raise/lower legacy import resource limits?

statement: ZIP adapter tests are only in-module unit tests with hand-built fixtures (13 tests); no integration tests in crates/entrybound/tests, no fuzz targets, no real-writer corpus, and no test loads tools/zip-compat/observed-outcomes-v1.json.
evidence_in_source: Grep of crates/*/tests found no zip/legacy references; no fuzz directory in repo
research_needed: Add cargo-fuzz targets for observe/resolve, a real-writer ZIP corpus (Info-ZIP, 7-Zip, Windows, macOS, Java, Python, Go, .NET), and a CI check against the observed-outcome matrix.

statement: 7z adapter owns all 7z structural interpretation; external codec crates only decode a packed byte stream after Entrybound validates the folder graph.

7z constants: 6-byte signature, 32-byte signature header, property IDs 0x00-0x19 (no kComment 0x16 handling), and method IDs COPY 00, LZMA 030101, LZMA2 21, BZip2 040202, DEFLATE 040108, Delta 03, BCJ x86 03030103; AES 06F10701, PPMd 030401, BCJ2 0303011B are named only for diagnostics.

SevenZImportPolicy is a public caller-owned struct of 20 limits covering source, Next Header, decoded header, files, folders, coders per folder, coder streams, packed streams, substreams per folder, coder property bytes, packed input, folder/file/total decoded bytes, expansion ratio, dictionary, observations, conflicts and resolutions.

Default 7z limits: source 16 GiB, Next Header and decoded header 64 MiB, 1M files/folders/packed streams/substreams, 8 coders and 16 coder streams per folder, 1 MiB properties, 8 GiB packed input, 4 GiB folder and single file, 16 GiB total, ratio 10000:1, dictionary 1 GiB, 8M observations. No measurement cited.
research_needed: Measure 7z corpus distribution (solid block sizes up to 4 GiB+ in ultra presets, dictionary sizes up to 1.5 GiB, header sizes) and peak RSS under defaults.
decision_needed: Are the 7z default limits frozen for v1, and do they admit 7-Zip ultra presets (dictionary 1536 MiB, solid blocks > 4 GiB)?

statement: Default max_folder_decoded_bytes 4 GiB and max_dictionary_bytes 1 GiB would refuse solid folders or LZMA2 dictionaries produced by 7-Zip's higher presets (large solid blocks, 1536 MiB dictionary on 64-bit ultra).
research_needed: Create archives with 7-Zip -mx9 -md=1536m and large -ms solid sizes; measure refusal and memory.

statement: Public 7z types: SevenZConversionReport (LOM, resolutions, synthesized ancestors, folder_count, solid_folder_count, coder_count, encoded_header), SevenZImportResult, and SevenZObservation exposing only lom(); streams, files and source stay private.
7z variable-length NUMBER decoding follows the 7z UINT64 prefix-bit scheme up to a 0xFF prefix plus eight bytes.
looks_like_sevenz(source) detects 7z by the 6-byte signature prefix only.
Only 7z format version major 0 with minor <= 4 is accepted; other versions are refused as unsupported by strict-v1.
research_needed: Confirm no current 7-Zip/p7zip/7-Zip-zstd release writes minor > 4.

statement: 7z Start Header CRC and Next Header CRC are mandatory integrity authorities (mismatch is Corrupt SevenZIntegrityMismatch); Next Header must lie within the source and end exactly at EOF, trailing bytes being structure errors.
Multi-volume (.7z.001) and archives with appended data after the Next Header are refused; SFX-prefixed 7z is not detected because the signature must start at offset 0.
evidence_in_source: docs/7z-import-v1.md L121-123 lists multi-volume as outside v1
research_needed: Measure prevalence of 7z SFX executables and split volumes in migration corpora.
decision_needed: Is 7z SFX/multi-volume import a v1 non-goal?

statement: Archive-scope 7z LOM fields: format major/minor, Next Header offset, size and CRC with exact signature-header byte locations.

Next Header may be empty (empty archive), a plain Header (0x01), or an Encoded Header (0x17) whose StreamsInfo is decoded through the same folder decoder in header mode, must yield exactly one substream within max_decoded_header_bytes, and is recorded with decoded size and SHA-256.
Nested encoded headers are refused: the decoded Encoded Header must begin with a plain Header NID.
research_needed: Check whether any 7z writer emits nested encoded headers.

statement: Encrypted 7z (AES-256 coder 06F10701), including encrypted headers, is refused with SevenZUnsupportedCoder; no password support exists.
evidence_in_source: docs/7z-import-v1.md L121 lists encrypted headers/content as outside v1
research_needed: Measure share of password-protected 7z in migration targets.
decision_needed: Is encrypted 7z import out of scope for v1?

statement: 7z packed streams must be exactly contiguous: main packed data must end where the encoded-header packed data (or Next Header) begins, and encoded-header packed data must end at the Next Header; any gap or overlap is Irreconcilable.
research_needed: Verify layouts from 7-Zip, p7zip, sevenz-rust2, py7zr, libarchive writers all satisfy contiguity.

statement: Many 7z LOM evidence locations are coarse or synthetic: coder/bind/count fields cite the whole Next Header extent, pack/unpack counts cite (source_base, cursor position), bitmap fields have zero length, and field_u64 raw_value is re-encoded little-endian rather than the source NUMBER bytes; decoded-header offsets are relative to the decoded buffer.
research_needed: Define exact-evidence requirements for 7z LOM before any 7z preserve mode; compare with ZIP exact raw bytes.
decision_needed: Must 7z LOM observations carry exact source byte locations and raw bytes like ZIP?

statement: 7z observe emits only Refinement conflicts: per EmptyStream file (EmptyStream+EmptyFile selects empty regular file, else directory) and per folder stream ownership (UnpackInfo vs SubStreamsInfo); no Omission/Divergence/Irreconcilable conflicts are recorded in the LOM.
The per-folder stream-ownership conflict records the folder's coder count as the UnpackInfo value compared with the substream count, which is not a like-for-like ownership claim.
research_needed: Review LOM semantics; replace with folder output count/size vs substream partition.

statement: 7z structural contradictions (missing sizes/names, pack count mismatch, name count mismatch, unmapped streams) are raised as SevenZConflictIrreconcilable diagnostics rather than LOM conflicts, and entry-kind/attribute disagreements are raised as SevenZConflictDivergence during resolve.
research_needed: Classify each 7z refusal into LOM conflict classes as groundwork for a future compat matrix (docs/7z-import-v1.md L116-117).

statement: 7z AdditionalStreamsInfo is refused as unsupported in strict-v1.
7z ArchiveProperties are recorded as raw-byte LOM fields 'archive.property-0xNN' without interpretation.

StreamsInfo must present PackInfo before UnpackInfo and SubStreamsInfo only after UnpackInfo without duplicates; folders require packed sizes; absent SubStreamsInfo implies one substream per folder carrying the folder CRC; required packed-stream count must equal PackInfo count.
PackInfo: pack position and stream count, each packed size bounded by max_packed_input_bytes, optional per-stream CRCs (verified during decode); sizes are mandatory.
External 7z folder definitions (external flag in UnpackInfo) are refused.
7z coder flags with alternative-method bits (0xC0) are refused.

Folder parsing bounds coder count (1..=8), total coder input/output streams (<=16) and property bytes; validates bind-pair indices, requires at least one packed input, and infers a single packed input when unambiguous.

Strict-v1 7z folders must be linear: one packed input, only 1-in/1-out coders, exactly coders-1 bind pairs, one core codec consuming packed data first, and at most one filter; BCJ2 (4-input), multi-filter chains (e.g. BCJ+Delta) and arbitrary graphs are refused.
research_needed: Measure BCJ2 prevalence (7-Zip default for x86 executables at -mx7+/older versions) and multi-filter chains in real 7z corpora.
decision_needed: Must BCJ2 and multi-filter folders be supported for v1 7z migration?

statement: Folder coder order is derived by walking from the packed input through bind pairs; multiply owned inputs, multiply bound outputs, missing inputs, cycles and disconnected coders are Irreconcilable.
The unit test named graph_cycles_and_unsupported_coders_are_stable only checks that a PPMd folder is refused with SevenZUnsupportedCoder; cycle detection is covered elsewhere.

Coder property validation before decode: COPY/BZip2/DEFLATE must have none; LZMA exactly 5 bytes with dictionary <= max_dictionary_bytes; LZMA2 one byte <= 40 with derived dictionary bound; Delta one byte; x86 BCJ empty or 4-byte start offset; others unsupported.

Supported 7z codecs are only COPY, LZMA, LZMA2, BZip2, DEFLATE with filters Delta and x86 BCJ; PPMd, BCJ2, ARM/ARM64/ARMT/PPC/SPARC/IA64/RISC-V filters, Deflate64, Zstandard/Brotli/LZ4 (7-Zip-zstd forks) and SWAP are refused with SevenZUnsupportedCoder.
research_needed: Corpus measurement of 7z coder usage (PPMd for text at -m0=PPMd, ARM64 filter in 7-Zip 23+ for ARM binaries, zstd forks).
decision_needed: Which additional 7z coders and filters must v1 decode?

statement: SubStreamsInfo: per-folder NumUnpackStream counts bounded by policy, sizes with last substream implied, substream CRCs omitted when a single substream inherits the folder CRC, and unused or missing CRC/size declarations are Irreconcilable.

FilesInfo parsing: file count bounded; Name, EmptyStream, EmptyFile, Anti, CTime, ATime, MTime, WinAttributes, StartPos and Dummy are recognised; each property must be consumed exactly; every file must have a name.
External (out-of-header) 7z file names and external time/attribute/start-position property data are refused as unsupported.

7z CTime, ATime, WinAttributes and StartPos are observed (StartPos bytes consumed without per-file observation) and reported as unsupported metadata classes legacy.7z.creation-time, access-time, windows-attributes, start-position.
research_needed: Decide mapping of 7z ctime/atime and Windows attributes (hidden/system/readonly) into canonical platform metadata.
decision_needed: Should 7z creation/access times and Windows attributes be imported into EAM platform metadata in v1?

statement: Dummy property must be all zero; unknown FilesInfo properties (including kComment 0x16) are recorded per file as raw bytes and as unsupported metadata legacy.7z.files-property-0xNN.
Unknown FilesInfo property bytes are copied into every file's observation list, so observation volume scales as files x property length and may exceed max_observations_per_subject or total budgets.
research_needed: Test a 100k-file archive with an unknown FilesInfo property; measure observation memory.

statement: 7z names are NUL-terminated UTF-16LE: odd byte length is a structure error, malformed UTF-16 (unpaired surrogates) or embedded NUL is SevenZUnsafePath, and name count must equal file count.
research_needed: Windows allows unpaired surrogates in NTFS names; measure frequency and decide whether raw-byte path components are needed.

statement: decode_streams verifies packed-stream CRCs, bounds each folder's declared output by folder (or header) limit and expansion ratio, decodes, verifies folder CRC, splits into substreams verifying each CRC, enforces total decoded bytes, and requires every packed stream and decoded byte to be used exactly once.
CRC checks run only when CRCs are declared; 7z folders or substreams without CRCs import silently with no integrity evidence and no FidelityReport or conflict noting the absence.
research_needed: Measure how often writers omit substream CRCs; decide whether absence should be reported.
decision_needed: Should missing 7z CRCs be surfaced in ConversionProvenance or FidelityReport?

statement: 7z import is fully in-memory: source copied into the observation, each folder decoded to a Vec, every substream copied again, and all plaintext retained until native planning; a 4 GiB solid folder needs at least 8 GiB transiently.
research_needed: Measure peak RSS for large solid 7z; evaluate streaming substream projection into the planner.
decision_needed: Must 7z import be bounded-memory for v1?

statement: decode_folder applies the core codec then an optional filter, requires decoded length to equal the final folder output size and re-checks expansion ratio; intermediate coder unpack sizes are not compared with actual intermediate output.
research_needed: Add a divergence check between the core coder's declared unpack size and the final size for filtered folders.

statement: Core decoders (lzma-rust2 LZMA/LZMA2, flate2 DEFLATE, bzip2 BZip2) decode at most declared size plus one byte and must consume exactly the packed stream; COPY requires packed size equal to declared size; trailing packed bytes are Irreconcilable.

Filters (Delta, x86 BCJ) are applied in place with lzma-rust2 StreamFilter; the decode return value is discarded and finish() output is not checked, so correctness for tail bytes relies on library behaviour tested only with one synthetic 81,920-byte buffer.
evidence_in_source: unit test generated_delta_and_x86_filters_are_exactly_inverted (L2892-2934); docs/7z-import-v1.md L110-113 claims 7-Zip 26.02 differential evidence not checked into tools/
research_needed: Differential tests against 7-Zip for BCJ/Delta with sizes not multiple of 4/5, buffers ending in E8/E9 opcodes, and large binaries; check in the 7z probe harness.

statement: The only continuously checked 7z oracle is sevenz-rust2 0.22.2 on a single LZMA2 encoded-header case; the 7-Zip 26.02 differential results cited by docs have no checked-in probe or outcome matrix (tools/ has zip-compat and tar-strict only).
research_needed: Check in a reproducible 7-Zip probe harness and observed-outcome file analogous to tools/zip-compat.

statement: resolve_strict decodes all streams, requires the number of stream-bearing files to equal decoded substreams, and assigns substreams to non-empty files in FilesInfo order with no leftovers.
7z anti-items (deletion markers from update archives) are refused as unsupported rather than projected.

7z entry kind: directory iff EmptyStream and not EmptyFile; when Windows attributes are present the directory bit 0x10 must agree, and stream-bearing entries marked directory are refused, both with SevenZConflictDivergence.
evidence_in_source: no unit test covers kind/attribute divergence
research_needed: Add tests for directory attribute disagreement and empty-file vs directory cases.

statement: 7z Windows reparse points/junctions (attribute 0x400), POSIX symlinks, FIFOs, character/block devices and other non-regular high-word mode kinds are refused with SevenZUnsupportedFeature.
evidence_in_source: docs/7z-import-v1.md L81-83; no unit test covers these refusals
research_needed: Measure symlink/reparse prevalence in 7z archives created with -snl on Linux/macOS/Windows.
decision_needed: Will 7z symlinks map to EAM symlink entries in v1?

statement: High-word POSIX mode is interpreted from attributes>>16 without checking 7-Zip's FILE_ATTRIBUTE_UNIX_EXTENSION flag (0x8000); Windows-only high attribute bits (e.g. RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS 0x400000, PINNED 0x80000) could be misread as executable bits or as device kinds and wrongly refused.
evidence_in_source: code reading; docs/7z-import-v1.md L83 says 'compatible high-word POSIX mode'
research_needed: Create 7z archives on Windows from OneDrive placeholders / pinned files and sequential-scan files; check executable flags and refusals versus 7-Zip.
decision_needed: Must the 0x8000 Unix-extension flag gate POSIX mode interpretation?

statement: Per-file plaintext is bounded by max_single_file_bytes and file bytes are summed against max_total_decoded_bytes during resolve (in addition to decode-time totals).
7z entries without MTime receive a placeholder mtime of Unix epoch 0 (non-restorable) and the FidelityReport still lists core.mtime as captured, so missing timestamps are not reported as unavailable.
research_needed: Check EAM/extraction behaviour for non-restorable epoch mtimes; add a fidelity test for archives lacking MTime.
decision_needed: Should absent 7z mtimes omit core.mtime and be reported as unavailable instead of a placeholder?

statement: 7z FILETIME mtimes convert to Unix seconds and nanoseconds with Euclidean division at 100 ns (Hectonanosecond) precision, marked restorable.
research_needed: Add unit tests for pre-1970 and far-future FILETIMEs (none exist).

statement: 7z path safety: empty, rooted ('/' or '\'), second byte ':' (drive), or NUL paths are SevenZUnsafePath; backslashes are normalised to '/'; any component containing ':' is refused as alternate-stream (SevenZUnsupportedFeature); empty, '.' and '..' components refused.
Normalising backslash to '/' means a POSIX-created 7z filename containing a literal backslash becomes a nested path, silently changing structure rather than being recorded as a conflict.
research_needed: Create 7z on Linux with 'a\b' filenames via p7zip/7-Zip; compare 7-Zip extraction on Linux vs Windows.

statement: 7z strict import refuses duplicate logical paths (DuplicateLogicalPath) and file-as-ancestor (FileAsAncestor); missing ancestors are synthesized as directories recorded as Omission resolutions.

7z resolutions include a Refinement '7z.structure-summary' recording folders, solid-folders (folders with >1 substreams) and coders; resolutions are sorted, deduplicated and bounded by max_resolutions.
7z EAM projection gives every non-synthesized entry executable and mtime metadata; files are Internal SHA-256 content refs; synthesized ancestors get empty metadata.

7z ConversionProvenance uses source_format '7z', adapter_id 'entrybound/sevenz-strict-v1', import_mode 'strict', no preservation record (None), and counts divergence/irreconcilable only from LOM conflicts (always zero on success).
7z supports only strict import: there are no compatibility profiles, no preservation mode, and no 7z export; public entry points are observe, resolve_strict and import_strict.
evidence_in_source: docs/7z-import-v1.md L121-123; CLI refuses --compat/--preserve for non-ZIP (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs L2280-2288)
research_needed: Build a 7z observed-outcome matrix (7-Zip, p7zip, libarchive, py7zr) before designing profiles.
decision_needed: Are 7z compat/preserve profiles and 7z export required for v1 or deferred?

statement: 7z FidelityReport: platform 'legacy:7z', captured core.executable, core.mtime and legacy.conversion-provenance; unavailable lists each unsupported metadata class; no degraded items.

7z reason codes: SevenZStructureInvalid (Nonconforming), TruncatedStream (Truncated), SevenZIntegrityMismatch (Corrupt), SevenZUnsupportedFeature and SevenZUnsupportedCoder (Unsupported, with hex method ID), SevenZConflictDivergence/Irreconcilable and SevenZUnsafePath (Nonconforming), LegacyResourcePolicyRefused (PolicyRefused).

7z structure errors use outcome class Nonconforming while ZIP structure errors use Corrupt, and 7z truncation uses generic TruncatedStream while ZIP uses ZipStructureInvalid; outcome-class mapping for malformed legacy input differs across adapters.
decision_needed: What outcome class should malformed foreign structure map to uniformly (Corrupt vs Nonconforming)?

statement: ZIP reason codes: LegacyResourcePolicyRefused (PolicyRefused), ZipStructureInvalid (Corrupt or Truncated), ZipUnsupportedFeature (Unsupported), ZipConflictDivergence, ZipConflictIrreconcilable, ZipAmbiguousName, ZipUnsafePath (Nonconforming); ZipCrcMismatch, ZipSizeMismatch (Corrupt); ZipOverlappingExtent and DuplicateLogicalPath, FileAsAncestor (Nonconforming).

7z adapter tests are 11 in-module unit tests with generated COPY fixtures and direct decoder calls; no integration tests, fuzz targets, real-writer corpus, BCJ/Delta end-to-end archive, anti-item, attribute-kind, FILETIME, or policy-limit tests exist.
evidence_in_source: Grep of crates/*/tests found no 7z references
research_needed: Add cargo-fuzz targets for 7z observe/resolve and a corpus from 7-Zip, p7zip, py7zr, sevenz-rust2, libarchive writers.

statement: Legacy decode dependencies are exact-pinned: bzip2 =0.6.1, crc32fast =1.5.0, flate2 =1.1.9, lzma-rust2 =0.20.0; sevenz-rust2 =0.22.2 is a dev-dependency used only as a test oracle.
research_needed: Dependency longevity/security review for lzma-rust2 and bzip2 crates (bzip2 0.6 may wrap C libbz2 or pure-Rust backend).

statement: Format-neutral strict import dispatch (legacy::import::import_strict) calls zip::import_strict and sevenz::import_strict with LegacyImportPolicy fields and adds 7z format statistics (folders, solid-folders, coders, encoded-header) to LegacyConversionReport.

Compatibility profiles are static rule tables compiled into the adapter; production code never executes a legacy runtime or re-parses source bytes per profile, and compatibility does not emulate runtime vulnerabilities (Entrybound safety stays enforced).
evidence_in_source: code structure; resolution text L744-747; docs/zip-compatibility-profiles-v1.md L3-5, L76-83
